title: automate-kms-hsm-tls-rotation-private-installer-helm-terraform-vault-sealed-secrets
author: Priya Nambiar
release_notes: Add automated KMS/HSM and TLS certificate rotation for Private Installer; Helm and Terraform modules updated to support Vault and SealedSecrets workflows; new upgrade/rollback hooks and smoke-tests. No breaking API changes. Admin action required to opt-in to automated rotation and provide KMS/HSM credentials via the new installer config.
description: Motivation: On-prem and VPC customers require automated lifecycle management for encryption keys and TLS certificates to meet compliance and reduce on-call burden. This PR implements an end-to-end automation flow for KMS/HSM key rotation and TLS certificate renewal for Private Installer deployments, with optional Vault and SealedSecrets integrations, Helm chart hooks, and Terraform module updates. Design summary: 1) KMS/HSM abstraction layer in the installer that supports Cloud KMS (GCP/AWS), customer-managed HSM via PKCS#11 or Cloud HSM, and a Vault-backed key-provider. 2) TLS rotation controller that can operate in two modes: operator-driven (installer-managed cron job + Kubernetes Job) and external (users bring their own ACME/Vault pipeline). 3) SealedSecrets and Vault support: new secrets-provider switch in values.yaml and installer config allowing persisted sealed secrets, automated unseal+reseal logic during rotation, and Vault transit integration for signing and wrapping keys. 4) Helm chart changes: introduce lifecycle hooks (pre-upgrade, post-upgrade, pre-delete) and templated Jobs for rotation, RBAC rules tightened for least privilege, and configurable job schedules. 5) Terraform updates: new module outputs/inputs to wire KMS/HSM credentials into installer bootstrap (e.g. vault_kms_role, hsm_key_label), and lifecycle resource to run one-time migration jobs during upgrade. 6) Upgrade/rollback tooling: migration hooks that create time-bound backup of both sealed-secrets and cert-manager resources, and a rollback script to revert secrets and re-initialize KV caches. Implementation notes: - Added installer pkg/kms with providers: aws_kms.go, gcp_kms.go, hsm_pkcs11.go, vault_transit.go and interfaces for RotateKey/ImportKey/Sign. - TLS controller implemented under pkg/rotation/tls_controller.go with support for cert-manager annotations and direct vault CSR flows. - Helm charts updated under charts/private-installer: values.yaml parameters rotation.enabled, rotation.mode, rotation.schedule, rotation.provider, rotation.hsmConfig. - Terraform module redwood-private-installer updated: modules/kms.tf, modules/vault.tf and examples to demonstrate HSM provisioning with SoftHSM for test clusters. - New e2e smoke tests under test/e2e/rotation that run in a local Kind+SoftHSM environment and validate rotation, unseal/reseal, and application connectivity. - Added CLI helper redwood-installer rotate-keys --dry-run and rotate-certificates commands for ops. Backwards compatibility and opt-in: Rotation is opt-in by default; existing installs remain unchanged unless rotation.enabled is set to true. Migration/upgrade path: - Step 1: upgrade the installer chart to include rotation CRDs and jobs (this PR adds Helm hooks to create those safely). - Step 2: run redwood-installer migrate-rotation which creates backup snapshots of sealed secrets and cert-manager resources into the configured storage (S3/GCS/MinIO). - Step 3: enable rotation in values and provide KMS/HSM credentials via Terraform outputs or Vault role. - Rollback notes: Helm pre-upgrade hooks create checkpointed resources and the installer exposes redwood-installer rollback-rotation to restore snapshots and reapply previous sealed secrets. Security & audit: - All key operations are logged to installer's audit log; Vault usage is configured to use wrapped responses; HSM paths require admin-provided PKCS#11 configuration. - RBAC tightened: rotation Jobs run in a dedicated namespace with minimal ServiceAccount permissions. Testing and validation: Unit tests for each provider, integration tests against SoftHSM and Vault dev server, and CI smoke tests added. Performance and safety: Rotation jobs are rate-limited to avoid bursting load; KV cache warmup ensures minimal latency impact. Known limitations: - HSM vendor drivers in production require customer provisioning; SoftHSM used for CI. - Automated certificate issuance via external ACME providers requires additional DNS automation out of scope. Related work: references ENG-4821 (rotation design), SEC-112 (audit requirements), and earlier PRs that added Vault/SealedSecrets support. Rollout plan: staged rollout to internal staging clusters for 2 weeks, then opt-in customers, then enable recommended defaults after 30 days. Documentation: updated docs/private-installer/rotation.md and added upgrade guide.

review_comments: Liam O'Connor: This looks comprehensive. Question: can we avoid storing unencrypted backups in S3? Suggest we use KMS-encrypted snapshots and provide an expiration TTL.
Priya Nambiar: Addressed. Snapshots are now written encrypted using the configured KMS provider and have configurable TTL. See terraform/modules/backup.tf and docs section.
Marta Ruiz: Need stronger failure semantics for partial rotation failures; how do we ensure we don't leave apps with mismatched secrets?
Priya Nambiar: Added transactional checkpoints and a preflight dry-run mode; rotation jobs will abort on partial failures and emit a rollback hook. See pkg/rotation/transaction.go and tests.
Chen Li: RBAC surface looks ok but reduce the SA permissions on secrets to get/list/watch only. Also add e2e test for re-encryption path.
Priya Nambiar: Reduced permissions and added e2e re-encryption test against SoftHSM and Vault dev server. CI now runs that test in the rotation suite.
Ops (internal): Verified on staging with SoftHSM; observed successful rotations and zero-downtime certificate reloads for nginx ingress controller.
merge_summary: Merged by squash-merge after 3 approvals (Liam, Marta, Chen). Merge notes: tagged release v1.12.0-private-installer, changelog updated, and prompting ops to run migration steps. No follow-up PR required. Backport not needed.
